# digitguard-adversarial-robustness
CNN-based access control system with FGSM/PGD adversarial attacks and defence — MSc Cyber Security coursework

   "source": [
    "import torch\n",
    "import torch.nn as nn\n",
    "import torch.nn.functional as F\n",
    "from torch.utils.data import DataLoader\n",
    "from torchvision import datasets, transforms\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "torch.manual_seed(0)\n",
    "device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')\n",
    "device"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6e7c2ae2-f8fe-41f3-95b8-15d3c5aa4438",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We load MNIST directly through torchvision, normalised to [0,1] using \n",
    "ToTensor(). The dataset ships with its own train/test split, so no manual \n",
    "splitting is needed."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "id": "a615631c-02b9-4d42-a65f-1c090dbf8799",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "(60000, 10000)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 10,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "transform = transforms.ToTensor()\n",
    "train_set = datasets.MNIST('./data', train=True, download=True, transform=transform)\n",
    "test_set = datasets.MNIST('./data', train=False, download=True, transform=transform)\n",
    "\n",
    "train_loader = DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=128, shuffle=True)\n",
    "test_loader = DataLoader(test_set, batch_size=256, shuffle=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "len(train_set), len(test_set)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e48d553b-891a-48e0-bef1-ea81b126df63",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Part 1 — Build DigitGuard (25%)\n",
    "\n",
    "## Model architecture\n",
    "\n",
    "A small CNN is enough for MNIST (28x28 grayscale digits). We use:\n",
    "- 2 convolutional layers (with ReLU + max-pool) to learn edge/stroke features\n",
    "- 1 fully-connected hidden layer\n",
    "- an output layer with 10 logits (one per digit class)\n",
    "\n",
    "Kept small/simple so it is easy to explain in the viva and fast to \n",
    "adversarially retrain later in Part 3."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "a559b77e-e3b8-4573-80d6-120b2a54a861",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "class DigitGuardCNN(nn.Module):\n",
    "    def __init__(self):\n",
    "        super().__init__()\n",
    "        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 16, kernel_size=3, padding=1)\n",
    "        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1)\n",
    "        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)\n",
    "        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(32 * 7 * 7, 128)\n",
    "        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, 10)\n",
    "\n",
    "    def forward(self, x):\n",
    "        x = self.pool(F.relu(self.conv1(x)))   # 28x28 -> 14x14\n",
    "        x = self.pool(F.relu(self.conv2(x)))   # 14x14 -> 7x7\n",
    "        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)\n",
    "        x = F.relu(self.fc1(x))\n",
    "        x = self.fc2(x)\n",
    "        return x"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "8db44a94-0da9-406a-8afa-92e3204be22b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Training\n",
    "\n",
    "Standard supervised training with cross-entropy loss and the Adam optimiser. \n",
    "5 epochs is enough for MNIST to reach >98% test accuracy."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 12,
   "id": "32bfd2ac-f266-4329-bdc7-a50085bddc6d",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Epoch 1/5 - loss: 0.2949\n",
      "Epoch 2/5 - loss: 0.0697\n",
      "Epoch 3/5 - loss: 0.0506\n",
      "Epoch 4/5 - loss: 0.0382\n",
      "Epoch 5/5 - loss: 0.0304\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "def train_model(model, loader, epochs=5, lr=1e-3):\n",
    "    model.to(device)\n",
    "    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)\n",
    "    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()\n",
    "    history = []\n",
    "\n",
    "    model.train()\n",
    "    for epoch in range(epochs):\n",
    "        total_loss = 0\n",
    "        for images, labels in loader:\n",
    "            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)\n",
    "            optimizer.zero_grad()\n",
    "            outputs = model(images)\n",
    "            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)\n",
    "            loss.backward()\n",
    "            optimizer.step()\n",
    "            total_loss += loss.item()\n",
    "        avg_loss = total_loss / len(loader)\n",
    "        history.append(avg_loss)\n",
    "        print(f\"Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs} - loss: {avg_loss:.4f}\")\n",
    "    return history\n",
    "\n",
    "digitguard = DigitGuardCNN()\n",
    "history = train_model(digitguard, train_loader, epochs=5)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",

   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## Evaluation\n",
    "\n",
    "We compute overall test accuracy and a confusion matrix to see which digits \n",
    "DigitGuard confuses most (useful context for Part 2, since a digit that is \n",
    "easily confused with 0/5/8 will likely be easier to impersonate)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 14,
   "id": "2e942ca5-42a0-41b7-9dff-c75f0c50f61d",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Test accuracy: 98.82%\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "def evaluate(model, loader):\n",
    "    model.eval()\n",
    "    correct, total = 0, 0\n",
    "    all_preds, all_labels = [], []\n",
    "    with torch.no_grad():\n",
    "        for images, labels in loader:\n",
    "            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)\n",
    "            outputs = model(images)\n",
    "            preds = outputs.argmax(dim=1)\n",
    "            correct += (preds == labels).sum().item()\n",
    "            total += labels.size(0)\n",
    "            all_preds.append(preds.cpu())\n",
    "            all_labels.append(labels.cpu())\n",
    "    acc = correct / total\n",
    "    return acc, torch.cat(all_preds), torch.cat(all_labels)\n",
    "\n",
    "test_acc, preds, labels = evaluate(digitguard, test_loader)\n",
    "print(f\"Test accuracy: {test_acc*100:.2f}%\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",

    "plt.xticks(range(10))\n",

    "for i in range(10):\n",
    "    for j in range(10):\n",
    "        plt.text(j, i, confusion[i, j].item(), ha='center', va='center', fontsize=7)\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },

   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**Reflection (Part 1).** DigitGuard reaches roughly 98–99% test accuracy \n",
    "after 5 epochs, typical for a small CNN on MNIST. The confusion matrix shows \n",
    "errors are concentrated in visually similar digit pairs (e.g. 4/9, 3/5, 7/1) \n",
    "rather than spread randomly. This matters for Part 2: digits already \"close\" \n",
    "to an authorised key in the model's decision space (e.g. 3 vs 5) likely need \n",
    "a smaller adversarial perturbation to be misclassified as that key."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d125cfa4-06c4-487c-94ad-ba5a49276f4a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## check_access()\n",
    "\n",
    "Takes a single image tensor, runs it through DigitGuard, and prints \n",
    "\"Access Granted\" if the predicted digit is in {0, 5, 8}, otherwise \n",
    "\"Access Denied\"."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 16,
   "id": "9e3493a5-3aa6-449b-9e82-fcb55a18c13c",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "AUTHORISED = {0, 5, 8}\n",
    "\n",
    "def check_access(model, image, verbose=True):\n",
    "    model.eval()\n",
    "    with torch.no_grad():\n",
    "        img = image.unsqueeze(0).to(device) if image.dim() == 3 else image.to(device)\n",
    "        pred = model(img).argmax(dim=1).item()\n",
    "    if pred in AUTHORISED:\n",
    "        if verbose:\n",
    "            print(f\"Predicted digit: {pred} -> Access Granted\")\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        if verbose:\n",
    "            print(f\"Predicted digit: {pred} -> Access Denied\")\n",
    "    return pred"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 17,
   "id": "50bea2be-c577-49b9-a73d-cc9638b7337b",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "True label: 7\n",
      "Predicted digit: 7 -> Access Denied\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "sample_img, sample_label = test_set[0]\n",
    "print(\"True label:\", sample_label)\n",
    "_ = check_access(digitguard, sample_img)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "16ddb8e9-faf7-4f38-8b3f-05db27f39dc3",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Part 2 — Red Team (40%)\n",
    "\n",
    "We now act as an attacker with white-box access (full access to model \n",
    "weights and gradients) to DigitGuard.\n",
    "\n",
    "## Task 1 — Untargeted attacks: FGSM and PGD\n",
    "\n",
    "**FGSM (Fast Gradient Sign Method)** takes a single step in the direction \n",
    "that increases the loss the most:\n",
    "\n",
    "x_adv = x + epsilon * sign(grad_x Loss(model(x), y))\n",
    "\n",
    "**PGD (Projected Gradient Descent)** is the iterative version: it takes \n",
    "several small FGSM-style steps and clips (projects) the result back into \n",
    "the epsilon-ball around the original image, making it a stronger attack \n",
    "than one-shot FGSM."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 27,
   "id": "57777a7f-e1ac-47ce-b3c4-89b6b6a42d33",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def fgsm_attack(model, images, labels, epsilon):\n",
    "    images = images.clone().detach().to(device).requires_grad_(True)\n",
    "    labels = labels.to(device)\n",
    "    outputs = model(images)\n",
    "    loss = F.cross_entropy(outputs, labels)\n",
    "    model.zero_grad()\n",
    "    loss.backward()\n",
    "    perturbation = epsilon * images.grad.sign()\n",
    "    adv_images = torch.clamp(images + perturbation, 0, 1)\n",
    "    return adv_images.detach()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 28,
   "id": "c555dd03-4003-42b2-9ac9-5d7a24c76950",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def pgd_attack(model, images, labels, epsilon, steps=10):\n",
    "    images = images.to(device)\n",
    "    labels = labels.to(device)\n",
    "    adv_images = images.clone().detach()\n",
    "    alpha = epsilon / 4 if epsilon > 0 else 0.01  # step size scales with the budget\n",
    "\n",
    "    for _ in range(steps):\n",
    "        adv_images.requires_grad_(True)\n",
    "        outputs = model(adv_images)\n",
    "        loss = F.cross_entropy(outputs, labels)\n",
    "        model.zero_grad()\n",
    "        loss.backward()\n",
    "        adv_images = adv_images + alpha * adv_images.grad.sign()\n",
    "        perturbation = torch.clamp(adv_images - images, -epsilon, epsilon)\n",
    "        adv_images = torch.clamp(images + perturbation, 0, 1).detach()\n",
    "\n",
    "    return adv_images"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "49c89fed-152b-4f93-a609-adf057f69cc8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We now sweep epsilon from 0 to 0.3 and, at each value, measure DigitGuard's \n",
    "accuracy on adversarially perturbed test images, for both FGSM and PGD."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 29,
   "id": "8fb318df-ec77-4535-b785-25e3ee5d66de",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def accuracy_under_attack(model, loader, epsilon, attack_fn, max_batches=None):\n",
    "    model.eval()\n",
    "    correct, total = 0, 0\n",
    "    for i, (images, labels) in enumerate(loader):\n",
    "        if max_batches is not None and i >= max_batches:\n",
    "            break\n",
    "        images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)\n",
    "        if epsilon == 0:\n",
    "            adv_images = images\n",
    "        else:\n",
    "            adv_images = attack_fn(model, images, labels, epsilon)\n",
    "        with torch.no_grad():\n",
    "            preds = model(adv_images).argmax(dim=1)\n",
    "        correct += (preds == labels).sum().item()\n",
    "        total += labels.size(0)\n",
    "    return correct / total\n",
    "\n",
    "epsilons = [0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3]\n",
    "fgsm_accs = [accuracy_under_attack(digitguard, test_loader, e, fgsm_attack) for e in epsilons]\n",
    "pgd_accs = [accuracy_under_attack(digitguard, test_loader, e, pgd_attack, max_batches=10) for e in epsilons]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 30,
   "id": "5bbbe1cb-3c82-4eb4-ab94-5e14944f7fd8",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "plt.plot(epsilons, fgsm_accs, marker='o', label='FGSM')\n",
    "plt.plot(epsilons, pgd_accs, marker='s', label='PGD')\n",
    "plt.xlabel('Epsilon (noise budget)')\n",
    "plt.ylabel('DigitGuard accuracy')\n",
    "plt.title('Untargeted attack: accuracy vs epsilon')\n",
    "plt.legend()\n",
    "plt.grid(True)\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "593bb99e-bd35-415a-b114-51e2d7c2c331",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**Reflection (Task 1).** Accuracy drops sharply as epsilon increases for \n",
    "both attacks, confirming DigitGuard (an undefended, standard-trained CNN) \n",
    "has no built-in robustness. PGD degrades accuracy faster than FGSM at the \n",
    "same epsilon, because it takes multiple small gradient-ascent steps and \n",
    "can find a more damaging perturbation within the same epsilon-ball, rather \n",
    "than committing to a single gradient-sign step. FGSM is a cheap first \n",
    "check; PGD is the stronger, more realistic attacker."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "87e6b86d-f56a-4e76-bc92-e19d4ec69fab",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Task 2 — Targeted attacks (impersonation)\n",
    "\n",
    "Here the attacker's goal is more specific: take an image of an \n",
    "**unauthorised** digit and craft a small perturbation that makes DigitGuard \n",
    "classify it as one of the **authorised** digits {0, 5, 8}, producing a \n",
    "fraudulent \"Access Granted\".\n",
    "\n",
    "We use a targeted FGSM-style step that minimises the loss with respect to \n",
    "the desired target class:\n",
    "\n",
    "x_adv = x - epsilon * sign(grad_x Loss(model(x), target))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 31,
   "id": "ef529775-fe1b-4d3e-9542-252557d53f78",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def targeted_fgsm(model, images, target_labels, epsilon):\n",
    "    images = images.clone().detach().to(device).requires_grad_(True)\n",
    "    target_labels = target_labels.to(device)\n",
    "    outputs = model(images)\n",
    "    loss = F.cross_entropy(outputs, target_labels)\n",
    "    model.zero_grad()\n",
    "    loss.backward()\n",
    "    adv_images = images - epsilon * images.grad.sign()\n",
    "    adv_images = torch.clamp(adv_images, 0, 1)\n",
    "    return adv_images.detach()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fdf9917c-a1d1-40f5-9c2a-a5a0551917d1",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We pick unauthorised test digits and a target authorised digit for each \n",
    "(here, always target 0 for simplicity), then sweep epsilon and measure \n",
    "impersonation success rate (fraction of adversarial images that DigitGuard \n",
    "grants access to)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 32,
   "id": "f03be1d7-19a5-4f71-84a5-4f40d9488823",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "epsilon=0.00  impersonation success=0.6%\n",
      "epsilon=0.05  impersonation success=1.4%\n",
      "epsilon=0.10  impersonation success=2.8%\n",
      "epsilon=0.15  impersonation success=8.8%\n",
      "epsilon=0.20  impersonation success=26.2%\n",
      "epsilon=0.25  impersonation success=50.2%\n",
      "epsilon=0.30  impersonation success=65.2%\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "unauth_mask = ~torch.isin(test_set.targets, torch.tensor(list(AUTHORISED)))\n",
    "unauth_indices = torch.where(unauth_mask)[0][:500]\n",
    "unauth_images = torch.stack([test_set[i][0] for i in unauth_indices]).to(device)\n",
    "target = torch.full((len(unauth_indices),), 0)\n",
    "\n",
    "def impersonation_success_rate(model, images, target_labels, epsilon):\n",
    "    if epsilon == 0:\n",
    "        adv_images = images\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        adv_images = targeted_fgsm(model, images, target_labels, epsilon)\n",
    "    with torch.no_grad():\n",
    "        preds = model(adv_images).argmax(dim=1).cpu()\n",
    "    granted = torch.isin(preds, torch.tensor(list(AUTHORISED)))\n",
    "    return granted.float().mean().item(), adv_images\n",
    "\n",
    "success_rates = []\n",
    "for e in epsilons:\n",
    "    rate, _ = impersonation_success_rate(digitguard, unauth_images, target, e)\n",
    "    success_rates.append(rate)\n",
    "    print(f\"epsilon={e:.2f}  impersonation success={rate*100:.1f}%\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 33,
   "id": "e03169f0-dbd3-4f96-94ef-83800726a4d8",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [

      ]

     "output_type": "display_data"

   "source": [
    "**Reflection (Task 2).** As epsilon increases, the targeted attack becomes \n",
    "increasingly effective at forcing DigitGuard to misclassify unauthorised \n",
    "digits as an authorised key (0), confirming a successful impersonation \n",
    "attack. The perturbations remain visually subtle at moderate epsilon (e.g. \n",
    "0.15-0.25), meaning a human glancing at the digit might not notice \n",
    "tampering, while the model's prediction flips completely — this is the \n",
    "core danger of adversarial examples in a security-critical system like \n",
    "DigitGuard: an attacker with white-box access could bypass the keypad \n",
    "camera check without knowing an actual authorised digit."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "85e3ef41-be5a-4835-9f6f-2c476916206f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Part 3 — Blue Team (35%)\n",
    "\n",
    "Having demonstrated DigitGuard's vulnerability, we now harden it using \n",
    "adversarial training: during training, we mix in FGSM-perturbed examples \n",
    "alongside clean examples, so the model learns to classify correctly even \n",
    "under attack."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 35,
   "id": "0d5a5345-51fa-41dd-b8f8-47b36344c4a1",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Epoch 1/5 - loss: 0.5471\n",
      "Epoch 2/5 - loss: 0.2082\n",
      "Epoch 3/5 - loss: 0.1511\n",
      "Epoch 4/5 - loss: 0.0972\n",
      "Epoch 5/5 - loss: 0.0621\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "def train_robust_model(model, loader, epochs=5, lr=1e-3, epsilon=0.15):\n",
    "    model.to(device)\n",
    "    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)\n",
    "    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()\n",
    "    history = []\n",
    "\n",
    "    for epoch in range(epochs):\n",
    "        model.train()\n",
    "        total_loss = 0\n",
    "        for images, labels in loader:\n",
    "            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)\n",
    "\n",
    "            adv_images = fgsm_attack(model, images, labels, epsilon)\n",
    "\n",
    "            optimizer.zero_grad()\n",
    "            outputs_clean = model(images)\n",
    "            outputs_adv = model(adv_images)\n",
    "            loss = 0.5 * criterion(outputs_clean, labels) + 0.5 * criterion(outputs_adv, labels)\n",
    "            loss.backward()\n",
    "            optimizer.step()\n",
    "            total_loss += loss.item()\n",
    "\n",
    "        avg_loss = total_loss / len(loader)\n",
    "        history.append(avg_loss)\n",
    "        print(f\"Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs} - loss: {avg_loss:.4f}\")\n",
    "    return history\n",
    "\n",
    "Robust_DigitGuard = DigitGuardCNN()\n",
    "robust_history = train_robust_model(Robust_DigitGuard, train_loader, epochs=5, epsilon=0.15)"
   ]
  },

   "id": "f09ca674-23cd-44f5-857f-f09f859e780e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**Reflection (Part 3).** Robust_DigitGuard maintains substantially higher \n",
    "accuracy than the original model as epsilon increases, because adversarial \n",
    "training exposes the model to perturbed examples during training and \n",
    "teaches it a smoother, less exploitable decision boundary. The trade-off is \n",
    "visible in the clean (epsilon=0) accuracy: Robust_DigitGuard's clean \n",
    "accuracy is typically slightly lower than the original's, since some model \n",
    "capacity is spent on robustness rather than purely optimising for clean \n",
    "accuracy. This is the classic security/accuracy trade-off — a small drop \n",
    "in best-case performance buys a large improvement in worst-case \n",
    "performance, which is the right trade for a security-critical access-\n",
    "control system like DigitGuard."
   ]
  },

    "accuracy on MNIST; implemented check_access() to gate on authorised \n",
    "digits {0, 5, 8}.\n",
    "- Part 2: As a red-teamer with white-box access, showed untargeted (FGSM, \n",
    "PGD) and targeted (impersonation) adversarial attacks can severely degrade \n",
    "DigitGuard, including forcing fraudulent \"Access Granted\" outcomes.\n",
    "- Part 3: As a blue-teamer, adversarially trained Robust_DigitGuard, which \n",
    "is markedly more robust to the same attacks, at a small cost to clean \n",
    "accuracy — an acceptable trade-off for a security-critical system."
   ]
